name: Binary Search Tree-Introduction
html:
Hey there. We are going to start with the last topic under "Basic Data Structures" i.e. Binary Search Tree.


Important Links : Introduction Video


Watch video WHAT

WHAT DO YOU THINK A BINARY SEARCH TREE IS?

A tree is said to be a Binary Search Tree if it fulfills the following conditions:

  1. It should be a Binary Tree, i.e. each node can have at most 2 children.
  2. The data of all the nodes to the left of any node should be lesser than the data of that node.
  3. The data of all the nodes to the right of any node should be greater than the data of that node.

Reader, meditate on the fact that the above properties must be true for all the nodes.

*You should also notice that these 3 properties are true for all the leaf nodes of a tree because a leaf node has no children.

Let's understand it through an example.

In figure 1, notice that each node has only 2 children and all the left nodes of any node are lesser in value than it is and all the right nodes of any node are greater in value than it is.

Let's tweak this tree a little and replace "40" with "51". Now it looks like figure 2.

Can you tell us if this tree is a Binary Search Tree?

You are right. It isn't. Because all the nodes in the left subtree of the root 50 should have a value less than 50. However, since 51 lies in the left subtree of 50 and has a value greater than 50, therefore it violates our properties. Hence, it is not a Binary Search Tree.

WHY

You must be thinking why do we even use a Binary Search Tree (BST). The answer lies in its name only. It is used for Searching.

Say, we are required to search a node 30 in the BST given in figure 1.

  • To do that, we start from the root of the tree and compare 30 with its value. Since 30<50, therefore it must lie to the left of 50. So we move to the left node 25 and discard the right subtree of 50.
  • Again we compare 30 with the current node 25. Since 30>25, then it must lie in the right subtree of 25. So, we move to the right node of 25 i.e. 37.
  • Here, 30<37, so we move to the right node of 37 i.e. 30.
  • Now we reach node 30. Since 30=30, therefore we have found our value.

The path of the above process is depicted by figure 3.

As you can see, the recursion of BST acts like a laser guide, i.e. it narrows our area for searching and runs straight to its target.

TIME COMPLEXITY

From the above discussion, we conclude that the time complexity of BST is O(log n).

Can you think why?

When we make the first comparison, we move toward one half of the subtree and discard the other half. Hence, the area to search gets reduced by half. Again that half area is further halved on the second comparison and so on.

We know from figure 4, that the time complexity is O (log n) when every subsequent element gets halved of its previous value.

BST vs BINARY TREE

The size and sum of both BST and Binary Tree have the same complexities because these functions are dependent on the structures of a tree and the structures of BST and BT are the same.

However, max, min and find functions depend upon the values of the nodes. Therefore, these functions are different for BST and BT.

Hence, as previously discussed, the time complexity of BST for these functions is O(log n) and the time complexity of BT is O(n).

We also want you to go through the introductory video of this topic for a better understanding.
